evals.prompt: I'm starting a new Go service called `invoice-service`. It needs to connect to MySQL, expose a REST API with Echo, and run a background job that reconciles invoices every 5 minutes. Use the private dependency injection pattern. Scaffold the full project layout and wire everything together in cmd/start.go.
evals.expected_output: A complete project skeleton: correct directory layout (cmd/, internal/app/, internal/http/, internal/worker/, internal/repository/, internal/service/, internal/usecase/, internal/models/, migrations/, etc.), app/db.go returning *sqlx.DB, app/repository.go with Repository struct + WithRepository(db), app/service.go with Service struct holding only external clients + WithServices(), app/usecase.go with Usecase struct + WithUsecases(repo, svc), handlers/handlers.go with Handlers struct + New(uc *app.Usecase), ticker job handler struct receiving *app.Usecase, cmd/start.go wiring db→repo→svc→uc→server/worker. No global app.A usage anywhere.
assertions: cmd/start.go calls WithDatabase, WithRepository, WithServices, and WithUsecases(repo, svc), then passes the usecase bundle to NewServer and the worker — no app.A access anywhere
internal/app/repository.go defines a Repository struct with a WithRepository(db *sqlx.DB) constructor
internal/app/service.go defines a Service struct that holds only external-dependency clients (no *sqlx.DB, no repositories)
internal/app/usecase.go defines a Usecase struct and a WithUsecases(repo, svc) constructor that combines repositories and services
internal/http/handlers/handlers.go defines a Handlers struct with a New constructor accepting *app.Usecase, and handler actions are methods on *Handlers
Worker job handler is a struct with the usecase bundle injected via constructor (e.g. NewReconcileInvoices(uc)), calling into the usecase layer — not repositories or services directly
No global var A or init()-based application struct in any app/ file

evals.prompt: Add a `client` domain to my existing Go service. I need: a Client model, a ClientRepository interface with Create/Get/Update/Delete methods and its sqlx implementation, a ClientUsecase with a Create flow, and four Echo HTTP handlers. Use the global singleton pattern (app.A). Follow the project style guide.
evals.expected_output: internal/models/client.go with db/json struct tags and nullable pointer fields; internal/repository/client.go with interface + private impl + constructor and ErrClientNotFound sentinel mapped from sql.ErrNoRows; internal/usecase/client.go with ClientUsecase interface + private impl + NewClientUsecase; four handler files (create_client.go, get_client.go, update_client.go, delete_client.go) each as plain functions using app.A.Usecase.Client; zap logging throughout.
assertions: models/client.go uses both `db:` and `json:` struct tags, with a nullable field as a pointer type (e.g. UpdatedAt *time.Time)

repository/client.go defines a Client interface with Create/Get/Update/Delete accepting context.Context as first param, plus a private implementation struct and a public constructor returning the interface
repository maps sql.ErrNoRows to a typed sentinel error (e.g. ErrClientNotFound)
usecase/client.go defines a ClientUsecase interface, a private implementation struct, and a NewClientUsecase constructor; Create wraps repo errors with fmt.Errorf and %w
Handler files are plain functions (not methods on a struct) and call the usecase via app.A.Usecase.Client — never app.A.Service or app.A.Repository directly
Logging uses zap (log.Logger.Error / log.Logger.Info), not fmt.Println or stdlib log

evals.prompt: My Go service needs to send a Telegram welcome message whenever a new client signs up. Build it following our Go conventions: a notifier client for the Telegram Bot API, and wire the send into the client-creation flow. If Telegram is down, client creation must still succeed.
evals.expected_output: internal/service/notifier/notifier.go with Notifier interface + private telegramNotifier + New(token) constructor returning the interface; pure external I/O with http.NewRequestWithContext, no DB imports; the usecase's Create flow injects both repository.Client and notifier.Notifier, calls notifier.Send after persisting, logs failure with zap and continues; handler calls only the usecase.
assertions: A new package internal/service/notifier/ (package notifier) is created with an interface, a private implementation struct, and a constructor returning the interface
The notifier package does not import sqlx, repository, or any database code — it performs external HTTP I/O with a context-aware request (http.NewRequestWithContext)
The usecase implementation receives BOTH repository.Client and notifier.Notifier via its constructor and calls notifier.Send inside the create flow
A notification failure is logged (zap) and NOT returned as an error — the client-creation flow continues and returns success
The HTTP handler calls only the usecase; the handler never touches the notifier or repository directly

evals.prompt: Show me how to write the JWT authentication middleware and the zap request-logging middleware for the Echo server, following our Go conventions. The logger middleware should skip /healthz and /metrics. Also show how they get registered in internal/http/server.go.
evals.expected_output: internal/http/middlewares/jwt_authentication.go and internal/http/middlewares/logger.go; ZapLogger accepts a *zap.Logger plus variadic skip URLs and returns echo.MiddlewareFunc; JWT middleware returns echo.ErrUnauthorized on failure; both registered in server.go before route definitions using e.Use().
assertions: Middleware files are in internal/http/middlewares/ package
ZapLogger accepts skipURLs variadic and skips logging for /healthz and /metrics
JWT middleware returns echo.ErrUnauthorized (not a custom error type) when token is missing or invalid
Both middlewares are registered via e.Use() in server.go before route groups are defined
Middleware functions return echo.MiddlewareFunc
